children: , the consumer-technology giant behind the iPhone, slid approximately 0.9% to $313.16 Wednesday ahead of its scheduled product event. The spotlight is on Apple's expected first foldable iPhoneand John Ternus's first major product launch since taking over as chief executive.

A foldable iPhone would push Apple into a fresh premium category, but it is arriving years after rivals began refining similar devices. The Associated Press noted that foldables still represent only a small slice of global smartphone sales. That puts pressure on Apple Intelligence to help sell the upgrade story rather than become another feature consumers can postpone.

Apple's latest financial statements show iPhone revenue of $54.25 billion, equal to 49.6% of quarterly sales, while inventory climbed to $11.09 billionroughly 94% above its September 2025 level. The valuation snapshot adds another warning: at $313.16, Apple trades 9.9% above its GF Value estimate of $284.95. A foldable hit could lift selling prices and reignite upgrades; a lukewarm launch would leave Apple carrying costly components while investors already pay a premium.

title: Apple Slides 1% Before Its First Foldable iPhone Test
